candidates.taskHardwareFit: GLM-5.3-Flash NVIDIA Kpool prefill tail seed; affected path requires NVIDIA accelerator evidence for runtime qualification; AMD is a regression control only
materiality: The NVIDIA prefill seed kernel addressed an aliased Kpool tail view using a dense block stride even though the tail shares the indexer's padded block stride.

A wrong write can leave the request tail unseeded while overwriting bytes in another request's persistent sparse-indexer cache, making this a silent cross-request cache-integrity defect rather than performance churn.
Upstream reproduced progressive corruption of a long-lived prefix-cached GLM-5.3-Flash prompt and repaired the kernel to use the runtime tensor strides.
deduplication: Distinct from Wave C vLLM PR #57317, which governed long-position KpoolTail slot mapping / out-of-bounds behavior rather than padded-stride prefill writes.
No qualification transfers from earlier GLM, KpoolTail, sparse-indexer, prefix-cache, or hardware receipts.
authorsClaims: Upstream reports a kernel-level sentinel reproduction on SM103, a known-bad predecessor failure, and corrected strided writes after the patch.
Upstream reports GLM-5.3-Flash TP4/GB300 end-to-end cache-corruption reproduction and request-level recovery after the patch.
disconfirmingEvidence: The reported GB300/SM103 results are upstream measurements, not SZL runtime receipts.
The affected behavior depends on an aliased, padded runtime cache layout and cannot be qualified by a dense synthetic tensor alone.
AMD already used stride-aware addressing, so an AMD pass does not qualify the NVIDIA defect path.
candidates.baseline: Exact predecessor source before db1bfdd4fb0dd7b8226402ee00abc7a987561b7c on the affected NVIDIA Kpool prefill-seed path, with prefix cache enabled and the real padded tail/indexer view.
requiredEvidence: Bind the exact vLLM source/build/container plus CUDA, Triton/compile stack and NVIDIA device identity actually exercised.
Bind the exact GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint/config/tokenizer bytes if full-model execution is performed; do not acquire or mirror weights merely for this wave.
Reproduce the known-bad predecessor with sentinel-filled aliased indexer/tail storage and prove that the predecessor writes outside the intended tail block while the candidate does not.
Exercise multiple tail block ids, low/high pool positions, multiple requests, prefix-cache hits, prefill-to-decode transition, cancellation, cache reset and worker restart.
Prove byte-level isolation: the selected tail block receives the exact K/score payload and no neighboring or foreign indexer/tail block changes unexpectedly.
When an already-available affected model/runtime exists, compare deterministic logits/outputs against an independent correct or cache-disabled reference before any throughput claim.
Use AMD only as a non-regression/control lane; never transfer AMD evidence into NVIDIA qualification.
Preserve rollback to the incumbent qualified backend or a configuration that disables the candidate Kpool path.
candidates.boundedResources: Start with no-weight deterministic kernel/cache fixtures in Forge; use already-available affected NVIDIA hardware through GPU Bridge only if present. New paid spend is zero.
candidates.rollback: Retain the incumbent qualified serving/backend configuration and disable the candidate Kpool path if byte isolation or output parity fails.

candidates.taskHardwareFit: SimpleCPUOffload scheduling/event metadata for hybrid KV layouts containing prefix-cacheable attention groups plus non-prefix-cacheable Kpool/QSA scratch groups
materiality: SimpleCPUOffload treated every KV group as offloadable even though GLM-5.3-Flash Kpool tail and QSA/circular-buffer scratch groups are explicitly non-prefix-cacheable.
Resolving request hashes at a scratch group's incompatible block size can trip a divisibility assertion and kill the engine on the first prefill store when KV cache events are enabled.
The repair excludes non-prefix-cacheable groups from store/load/hash/event metadata while preserving cacheable attention-group offload and BlockStored evidence.
deduplication: Distinct from Wave C vLLM PR #57160, which governed ROCm CPU-offload mmap/pinned-memory startup behavior rather than cache-group eligibility and hash/event semantics.

Distinct from this wave's PR #57477 padded-stride corruption; one concerns whether a scratch group participates in offload/hash metadata and the other concerns where NVIDIA Kpool seed bytes are written.
No qualification transfers from other offload, GLM, Kpool, QSA, cache-event, or accelerator receipts.
authorsClaims: Upstream reports deterministic scheduler/event tests for prefix-cacheable plus scratch groups and an end-to-end GLM-5.3-Flash TP4/EP store/load run on 4x GB300.
Upstream reports that CPU-hit output deltas were within the fresh-recompute/GPU-hit variability observed in its test setup.
disconfirmingEvidence: The 4x GB300 model run and accuracy table are upstream measurements, not SZL runtime or model-quality receipts.
A successful source-level scheduler fixture cannot establish full-model accelerator correctness, provider publication, or production readiness.
Non-prefix-cacheable scratch groups intentionally have no durable hash identity; silently inventing one would violate the fix's contract.
candidates.baseline: Exact predecessor SimpleCPUOffload scheduler before f648eed23dc48fcc8ba64be0c4182f8e775b5bfa with a cacheable attention group plus an incompatible non-prefix-cacheable scratch group and KV events enabled.
requiredEvidence: Bind the exact vLLM source/build used by every executed scheduler or model fixture.

Reproduce the known-bad predecessor divisibility/assertion failure using a FullAttention group plus Kpool/QSA-like non-prefix-cacheable scratch group whose block size is incompatible with the hash block size.
Prove scratch blocks never enter prefix-cache store/load pairs, request hash resolution, durable cache-hit accounting, or BlockStored/Removed event claims.
Prove cacheable attention groups still store, load and emit exact event metadata with events enabled and disabled, including first prefill, hit, miss, eviction/reset and restart cases.
Exercise eager and any admitted lazy offload mode separately; unexercised modes remain UNQUALIFIED.
Use deterministic store/load byte identity and token/block accounting before interpreting output parity or performance.

If an already-available GLM-5.3-Flash runtime is used, bind exact checkpoint/runtime/hardware identities and compare cache-disabled, GPU-hit and CPU-hit behavior under predeclared tolerances; otherwise keep model-level runtime evidence UNAVAILABLE.
Preserve rollback by disabling SimpleCPUOffload or reverting to the incumbent qualified connector/runtime path.
candidates.boundedResources: Forge can execute no-weight scheduler/event fixtures locally; real-model accelerator closure is optional and only on already-available hardware through GPU Bridge. New paid spend is zero.
candidates.rollback: Disable SimpleCPUOffload or retain the incumbent qualified cache connector if eligibility, event integrity, or output evidence fails.
